lesson.title: Play the Point
lesson.hook: Three shots, your calls. Each choice decides what happens next.
lesson.memHTML: Serve to open it. Hit behind them to finish it.
lesson.tomorrow: Before your next service game, plan two shots: serve wide, then hit into the open court.

bp1.name: Your serve
bp1.sit: Your serve. They're standing guard in the middle, ready for it.
opts: Down the T, into the middle

lines.A: They stay central and hit a deep return. Your point to play, but no opening yet.
lines.B: It pulls them off the court. They block it back short: the court is open.

bp1.payoff: The wide serve pulled them off the court and set up your next shot.
bp1.principle: Serve to open the court, not just to start the point.
bp1.why: A serve down the T keeps the returner in the middle, where every shot is easy to cover. A wide serve moves them before the rally starts.
bp1.take: Serve to open the court, not just to start the point.

bp1A.name: After a deep return
bp1A.sit: Their return comes back deep. They're back in the middle and set.
bp1A.q: Where does your next ball go?

lines.A: It lands in their strike zone. They hit through it. Back to even.
lines.B: They have to run for it and can only float it back. You're set early.
lines.C: It goes where they already are. They take a full swing. Back to even.

bp1A.payoff: Even from a deep return, the open corner made them run and float it back.
bp1A.principle: Make them move before you try to finish.
bp1A.why: A ball to the middle, or back to them, lets them swing from balance. The open corner makes them hit on the run, and running players float it back.
bp1A.take: Hit your next ball where they aren't, before trying to finish.

bp1B.name: After a short return
bp1B.sit: Their blocked return lands short. They're still out wide, scrambling back.
bp1B.q: Where does your next ball go?

lines.A: It lands where they're heading. They get there and hit it hard. Back to even.
lines.B: The court is empty. They reach it at a full sprint and can only float it back.
lines.C: It goes back to the side they're on. They take a full swing. Back to even.

bp1B.payoff: Your serve opened the court and your next ball went straight into it.
bp1B.principle: The serve opens the court; the next ball uses it.
bp1B.why: They're still out wide from the serve. Into the open corner, they have the whole court to run and only a float to hit.
bp1B.take: After a wide serve, the next ball goes into the open court.

bp2AB.name: Their float
bp2AB.sit: Their float sits up. They're sprinting back towards the middle.

lines.A: They get there and chip it back. Still your point, but not finished.
lines.B: It meets them on the way back. Back to even.
lines.C: They turn back and chip it. Still yours, but a T serve never opened enough.

bp2AB.payoff: You kept control, but after a T serve they were never far enough off the court for a winner.
bp2AB.why: They're sprinting back to the middle. Hitting where they're going lets them arrive and play; hitting behind them makes them stop, turn and go back, and nobody does that in time.
bp2AB.take: When they're sprinting back, hit behind them.

bp2BB.name: Their float
bp2BB.sit: Their float sits up. They're sprinting back towards the middle.

lines.A: Into their run. They get there and chip it back. Still your point, not finished.
lines.B: It meets them on the way back. Back to even.
lines.C: They're running the other way and can't turn in time. Winner.

bp2BB.payoff: Serve wide, open corner, behind them: you built that winner in three shots.
bp2BB.why: They're sprinting back to the middle. Hitting where they're going lets them arrive and play; hitting behind them makes them stop, turn and go back, and nobody does that in time.
bp2BB.take: When they're sprinting back, hit behind them.
